correctness.rationale: Projection onto the real constants gives E4−E2² in the denominator, and Fock orthogonality removes exactly |a|⁴ from E4 in the numerator. The quotient decreases strictly in E4 at fixed magnitudes for every nonconstant F, forcing negative interference if all coefficients are nonzero. Vanishing c gives the affine ratio 2; vanishing a or b cannot exceed 2 by the moment expansion. In the rotated and scaled form x+z−yz², the x-derivative changes from positive to negative at the unique positive root of Q. Its maximum profile exceeds 2 and tends to 2 at both ends of y>0, so an interior maximizer exists. An independently implemented coefficient convolution and Sylvester determinant check verifies the stationary equations and the displayed resultant. Its only positive y candidate gives exactly one normalized optimizer; undoing the two symmetries yields the stated orbit, in addition to trivial equality for constants. Independent root isolation and evaluation give C₂=1.563357712046434710589791267846703625912… .
residual_risks: The sharp result and equality classification are only for degree at most two; the full Fock-space optimum is not determined.
